newsitem.title: USA: U.S. sets airbag announcement for Friday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sets airbag announcement for Friday.

text.p: The U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said on Thursday it would make an announcment on car airbags on Friday at 1030 EST/1530 GMT.
The NHTSA has been weighing proposals to amend its airbag regulations to better protect children and smaller adults.
While credited with saving more than 1,100 lives the past 10 years, airbags are also blamed for killing some 30 children and 10 smaller adults.
The deaths have been blamed on the high velocity of inflation of the front-seat airbags.

Among the proposals being considered by the NHTSA are to reduce the speed of inflation and to mandate the installation of dual-speed bags that would inflate rapidly in high-speed crashes but at slower speeds in less severe crashes.

The decision is expected to be an interim move until the car industry developes "smart" airbags that would "sense" when a child or smaller adult is in the passenger seat and reduce the speed of inflation accordingly.
